# Oncobase

> Oncobase is an open-source (MIT) knowledge base for taking control of your care. Publish a vault of markdown notes, papers, and results to a searchable reader with AI search and chat, role-based privacy, inline redaction, and clinical viewers.

It was inspired by Sid Sijbrandij's osteosarc.com (https://osteosarc.com/).

## Start here

- [Everything Oncobase can do](https://diana-tnbc.com/features): the public features page.
- [Full feature and interface list for agents](https://diana-tnbc.com/llms-full.txt): every feature, where it lives, and how to call it.
- [Source code and README](https://github.com/jasonLaster/oncobase): MIT licensed.
- [Diana's knowledge base](https://diana-tnbc.com/): the first site built on Oncobase.

## What it does

- Read: Find your way around and read comfortably, on any screen.
- Ask: Search by meaning, or talk to the knowledge base.
- Protect: Share the science without sharing the patient.
- See the data: Timelines, scans, and slides next to the notes.
- Share: Bring family, doctors, and researchers in.
- Build: Publish from plain files. Extend it with code or agents.

## Notes for agents

- The reader is a client-rendered web app; most content needs a signed-in session or the site password.
- The public guides at https://diana-tnbc.com/education and the features page need no password.
- To publish, use the `oncobase` CLI (`oncobase check`, then `oncobase publish`) and the bundled skills (`oncobase skills`).
